name: Relative Peeling Is Preserved by Coordinate-Block Replacement
statement: For nonempty ample $T\subseteq H$ with marked coordinate $z$, $W_E(H)$ peels to $W_E(T)$ exactly when $H$ peels to $T$. If $H$ is an ample forbidden class, $|E|\ge2$, and $e\in E$, then the $e=b$ section of $W_E(H)$ peels to its $e$-reduction exactly when the old section $B_b$ peels to the old overlap $A=B_0\cap B_1$. For every coordinate outside the replaced block, relative peelability of either section to its reduction is also unchanged.
proof: The corner-lifting construction for block replacement applies to any deletion prefix and can stop when $T$ remains. Conversely, reduce all but one block coordinate; the images of a relative corner sequence are ample and consecutive images either agree or differ by one concept, so removing repetitions gives a relative sequence from $H$ to $T$. For a new coordinate in a binary block, the deletable vertices are precisely the lifts of $B_b\setminus A$, and their corner cubes correspond term by term to the old section corner cubes. Larger blocks reduce to this binary pair by replacement of the other coordinate. Old-coordinate sections and reductions commute with replacement, so the general equivalence applies directly.
